dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: This isn't a place anyone can just wander into, trespasser.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I leave it to you to help Sorush out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Sign of Apaosha...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: The appearance of the Sign of Apaosha is a result of the constant build-up of defilement.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: The last time such an occurrence happened was centuries ago. I, along with some human warriors, set about eradicating it.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Should the defilement be allowed to erode the structure of the Harvisptokhm, then once the filth grows too much for the Khvarena to contain, the Tunigi Hollow's rift might just reopen.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Pari...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: We Pari exist to avert the catastrophe and cleanse the defilement.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: The divine bird Simurgh drank the Amrita and mixed her Khvarena with the water's essence, thus creating countless beings.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Amongst the countless motes of Khvarena, the ones blessed with sentience are us, the Pari.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Our power comes from the primordial Amrita, and one day, so too will our power flow back to its source.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Sorush...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Don't mind her tough talk. She is a good petal at heart.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Sorush was born after the dust of the previous catastrophe settled, and hasn't witnessed the war of old. Hence, she holds many fantasies as to how things were.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: However, every Pari has a fated responsibility. From this perspective, she is unique. Even I cannot fully comprehend the mysteries of the Khvarena...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's alright.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Then, I wish you the best and look forward to hearing the good news!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Ah. We meet again. Did you miss me that much?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Sign of Apaosha...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Thanks to you, the Sign of Apaosha has been entirely extinguished.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Although the power of the defilement can never be fully eradicated, should it wish to return and infest this place, then it may just take a little longer yet.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: We Pari will also take this chance to rest and recuperate.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Pari...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: We Pari exist to avert the catastrophe and cleanse the defilement.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: The divine bird Simurgh drank the Amrita and mixed her Khvarena with the water's essence, thus creating countless beings.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Amongst the countless motes of Khvarena, the ones blessed with sentience are us, the Pari.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Our power comes from the primordial Amrita, and one day, so too will our power flow back to its source.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Sorush...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Ah, Sorush has grown quite a bit. It seems she is indeed worthy of the Bloomguard title. Of course, much of this is thanks to your influence.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Please continue to instruct her for what is to come.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the former generations of the Order of Skeptics...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: They claimed to be those that once fought side by side with the heroes of Dahri.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Although I never met any Dahri aside from that swordsman, any who face the beasts of corruption stands as our ally.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Our battle against the defilement will continue on forever. In the face of such an ever-lasting conflict, the regards of humanity is meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: We shall meet again.
